drug_class: Prostaglandin analog (eye pressure-lowering agent / eyelash growth agent)
purpose: Bimatoprost is mainly used as eye drops to lower pressure inside the eye in people with glaucoma or high eye pressure. Lowering eye pressure helps protect your vision and prevents damage to the optic nerve. It is also used under the brand name Latisse to help grow longer, thicker, and darker eyelashes.
how_it_works: Your eye constantly makes and drains a fluid called aqueous humor. In glaucoma, this fluid does not drain well enough, which raises pressure inside the eye. Bimatoprost works by helping that fluid drain out more easily, which lowers the pressure and keeps your eye healthier.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include redness of the eye, itching, or a feeling like something is in your eye. You may also notice your eyelashes getting longer or thicker, and the skin around your eye or your iris (the colored part of your eye) may gradually get darker over time. This color change can be permanent.
warnings: Do not use this medication if you are allergic to bimatoprost or any ingredient in the drops. Tell your doctor if you wear contact lenses — you should remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each one. Let your doctor know if you have ever had eye surgery, eye infections, or any other eye problems. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: For glaucoma (Lumigan): Place one drop into the affected eye(s) once every evening. For eyelash growth (Latisse): Apply one drop along the upper eyelid skin at the base of the eyelashes once nightly using the applicator provided. Never use more than directed, as using it more often can actually make it less effective.
